BBC Sport - Edin Dzeko: Roma sign Man City striker on season-long loan

The press seem to be missing a trick here - it's a loan with an obligation to buy in the same way Jovetic, Nastasic, Negredo and others are. Personally I don't really like it but the men at the top seem to think it's a good idea so whatever.

He's always been a bit of a strange one Edin Dzeko, in as much as most City fans didn't like him and grew frustrated with him. His first touch is awful and in a team built on the foundations of the possession game he stuck out like a sore thumb. On the other side though he is the King of Excuseville from other fans, a little like Balotelli seems to be amongst Liverpool fans now (which obviously isn't their fault).

Firstly the problem with his inconsistency was that he didn't get a run of games. Until he got a run of games and was still inconsistent. Then it was the system we played which "lacked width" because we didn't use out and out wingers, instead replacing them with wing backs - he could only play in a team that had wingers. Until we got a team with wingers and he still wasn't a consistently good player. Then it was the manager, but we got a new manager and he still didn't make that breakthrough. Then it went back to game time.

My somewhat laboured point here is that Dzeko is one of those players who is frustrating because he's like the Mona Lisa laughing - obviously a work of art and appreciated but still not quite right. The devil is always in the details and that's Dzeko's biggest failing for us; he can score goals but not enough to kick out Aguero, has absolutely world class Iniesta level vision for a through ball pass but rarely uses it, is a big fit lad with loads of energy but walks around the pitch and doesn't play the channels enough for a lone striker.

Dzeko going to me is the true signal that this is the start of City's Third Generation since the takeover 7 years ago. We wanted to get into the CL so we built a team for that consisting of the Adebayors, Bellamys, Bridges, Kolos, De Jongs, and Givens. Then we achieved this and then wanted to build a squad capable of winning the title which consisted of Yaya, Silva, Tevez, Aguero, Nasri and the like of which we achieved twice in four years. Now we seem to be building a team capable of winning the CL with massive money purchases like Sterling and De Bruyne. We finally seem to be going for the highest available quality regardless of price rather than sacrificing and buying players who are really good but not great.

Unfortunately for Edin, I think he's the level of a team that could easily win the CL but not consistently go to the semis and final if that makes sense. Closer to a Juve and Dortmund rather than to a Bayern and Barca. Still think he's a better option than Bony for our team, who I'm worried about the performances of and am wondering if his relationship with Yaya was seen as a positive trait in him staying, but we have an embarrassment of riches at youth level in and the financial power to go out and grab another if needed.

The switch to a Barcelona like 4-3-3 which seems to be coming would render Edin as surplus even without the remarkable progress Kelechi Ihenacho has made, firmly putting him down as a first team squad member

He scored some points winning goals for us and obviously he'll be fondly remembered for the first goal against QPR in the 93:20 aswell as the demolition of United in the 6-1, but overall we're a better team without him and he was disappointing performance wise far more than he wasn't. The old joke amongst the fans is that every time Dzeko has a terrible game he seems to score which is a laugh but also doesn't count the amount of chances that the rest of the team could have scored if we had a player performing up front.

Overall I get the feeling that Edin Dzeko will become City's Roy Keane. For years ahead now every time we have a bad result then people will completely ignore his obvious flaws that they know about now, and he'll become this lethal goalscorer who would always nick a goal in a tight game. Like Keane, we'll be talking about how we've never replaced him for years though miss the obvious answer that he wasn't replaced because the whole system of football has changed and his type of player is no longer needed
